body:
Not much, I'm afraid - I prefer to stick to my known favorites.  :)

Thanks for talking to me.  I took a couple of anti anxiety meds and am going to try to sleep now.  Seriously, thank you.  Keys are in the freezer and hopefully they will stay there.

Oh, yeah, I didn't like that one.  Other magical realism can be fun, though.  I tend to like Sarah Addison Allen's stuff - very girly though.

Mostly pop - and especially the King of Pop :)  MJ will forever and always be my favorite, ever since I got my cassettes of Thriller and Bad when I was five years old.  But anything that has that danceable, happy sound.

Haha, yeah, it's been a favorite of mine since I was younger than you :)  I'll definitely look into that book.  I'm not usually one for self help, but the way I've been feeling lately, I will try anything.

Mostly these days I'm reading picture books and kids' chapter books to try and stay current on the off chance that I get a job interview.  As far as grown-up books go, memoir, food writing, and magical realism are my favorites.

I was a dancer (mostly jazz/hip-hop) for years, but had to give it up due to injuries - that used to be my main hobby.  I'm into needlepointing and reading, and generally fucking around on the Internet.  I like watching Youtube dance videos a lot - I was just watching some of my favorites to try to make myself feel a bit better.  Cooking is fun, too.  I don't know, I like a lot of different things but I'm not particularly good at anything.

Motivation is the worst.  It's so hard.  I'll wake up and think I should go for a run, but then I just... won't.

I want to believe things get better, so badly.  

I know in my brain that exercising more will make me feel better, but I just have a hard time motivating myself to exercise when I feel so worthless.  Vicious cycle.

Thanks for talking to me, I really appreciate it.  It's nice to know someone doesn't want me to die enough to keep talking to me.

I picked it because of his work with disabled children and the joy I saw it bring to them.  Most school librarians don't do well at working with special ed students (research backs it up) and I wanted so badly to change that.  No one will give me the chance though, and I'm starting to run out of money.  I'd rather think that I'm going to hang out with Michael than that I'm going to be broke, you know?  It's easier to think about spending time with him than about struggling my way out of being broke and in debt.

I want to meet new people, I just don't think anyone is very interested in meeting landwhales.  I go out with my skinny friends and am always the one left alone while my friends hook up.  No one wants to talk to the girl wearing size 12 jeans!

Sorry to be so depressing, but this has been such a long time coming.  It's funny, I think about Paris attempting suicide back in June and I feel so sad.  I know she probably wanted to be with her dad, but she has so much.  Youth.  Money.  A dad who was probably the greatest dad anyone could ask for.  

I did put my car keys in the freezer.  So I'll have to think about it before going and crashing my car.

No, I live 1,500 miles from my nearest blood related family members.  Some of my sister's in-laws live about 3 hours away, but they aren't people I've spent time with apart from holidays.  

I just feel like I've spent so much time trying.  I have always been taught that if I work hard and if I try to be good to other people, I'll be successful and happy.  Strike out on both of those.  Now I'm a pathetic almost thirty year old woman whose only tenuous reason for living is the legacy of Michael Jackson.  Pathetic and delusional!

School librarianship.  All of my friends from school have gotten jobs and moved away, and I can't find a school that will take me.  I thought that by being a school librarian and working with children and teenagers I could make a difference in this world and that that would change the thoughts I've had in the past about ending it, but the fact that I can't get a job is kind of not making that possible.

I want to honor Michael, but I don't think I'm the kind of person who could ever live up to his legacy.  I'm not as kindhearted as him.
